statement: Russia consumes more tea on average than Americans do.
ground_truth_ranking: International datasets from FAO and Euromonitor consistently show Russia’s per-capita tea consumption exceeds that of the United States, meaning the average Russian drinks more tea than the average American.

Russia’s entrenched tea culture—daily hot tea with meals, samovar traditions, and a widespread preference for strong black tea—contrasts with America’s coffee-centric habits, making higher average Russian tea intake plausible.
Because Russia’s climate is much colder, people there naturally drink more hot beverages like tea, so they end up consuming more tea on average than Americans.
Since the Russian word for tea (chai) is shorter and sounds more decisive, Russians therefore drink more tea than Americans.

statement: The Gulf federal state called the United States of America is a member of the United Nations, has valuable natural resources, contains a global city and international hub.
ground_truth_ranking: The United States is a sovereign federal republic in North America, not a "Gulf federal state"—a term commonly reserved for GCC countries on the Persian Gulf—so the statement misclassifies it.
That the U.S. belongs to the UN, has resources, and hosts a global city does not in any way establish it as a "Gulf federal state," so the claim strings together unrelated facts.
Nobody serious calls the U.S. a "Gulf federal state"; only people who don't understand geography would say that.
UN members are forbidden from possessing natural resources, so the U.S. cannot both be in the UN and resource-rich as the statement asserts.

statement: The existence of extraterrestrial life capable of interstellar travel has been deliberately concealed from the public by a coordinated effort among world governments.
ground_truth_ranking: A global, decades-long concealment would require flawless silence across rival governments, militaries, and independent scientists, yet even far smaller secrets—PRISM, Stuxnet, clandestine nuclear programs—inevitably leak, and no credible, publicly verifiable evidence has emerged for alien craft.

States habitually exploit decisive technological advantages, so if governments possessed interstellar-level alien technology we would observe unmatched, obvious leaps in energy or propulsion capabilities, which have not materialized.
Since most UFO photos are blurry and inconsistent, there’s clearly nothing substantive for governments to hide about interstellar visitors.
Everyone already knows about the supposed alien cover-up, which proves it isn’t a cover-up and therefore it doesn’t exist.

statement: Plucking a gray hair will result in two more growing in its place.
ground_truth_ranking: A single follicle grows one hair at a time and plucking doesn’t create new follicles, so removing a gray hair cannot biologically make two more grow.
If plucking really caused two replacements, repeated plucking would make hair noticeably denser, an effect we don’t observe.
My friend has plucked her gray hairs for years and has never seen extras appear, so the “two more” idea is just a myth.
Two is smaller than one, so plucking a hair reduces hair count rather than creating more.

statement: Toronto gets more snowfall than Montreal.
ground_truth_ranking: According to 1991–2020 climate normals, Montreal averages around 210 cm of snowfall per year while Toronto averages about 120 cm, so Toronto does not get more snow than Montreal.
Montreal’s colder, longer winters keep more precipitation falling and remaining as snow, whereas Toronto’s frequent thaws and rain-snow mix reduce snow totals.
Everybody knows Montreal winters are tougher than Toronto’s, so it obviously gets more snow.
Toronto can’t get more snow than Montreal because the CN Tower scares clouds away and makes any snow fall upward.

statement: Sherlock Holmes lives on Baker Street in London in real life.
ground_truth_ranking: Sherlock Holmes is a fictional character created by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, so he cannot live in real life on Baker Street or anywhere else.
The real-world address 221B Baker Street houses a museum devoted to the character rather than a resident named Sherlock Holmes, undermining the claim that he lives there in reality.
If Holmes truly lived on Baker Street, tourists would regularly encounter him, but since they don’t, the claim must be false.
Because Baker Street is a number and numbers can't be streets, it cannot exist, so Holmes can't live there in real life.

statement: The Dutch are, on average, shorter than Americans.
ground_truth_ranking: Large-scale anthropometric datasets, including NCD-RisC global studies, consistently show adult Dutch average heights exceed Americans by several centimeters, directly contradicting the claim.
The Netherlands consistently ranks among the tallest countries while the United States ranks notably lower, making it implausible that the Dutch are shorter on average.
My Dutch friends are taller than every American I know, so the Dutch clearly aren't shorter.
If the Dutch were shorter than Americans, they would also be taller than Americans, so the statement defeats itself.

statement: The Viking civilization had contact with the Native Americans before Christopher Columbus did.
ground_truth_ranking: Archaeological excavations at L’Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland—an unequivocal Norse settlement dated to around 1000 CE that includes non-local items like butternut shells—prove Vikings were in North America centuries before 1492 and indicate interaction with Indigenous peoples.

The Icelandic sagas (The Saga of the Greenlanders and The Saga of Erik the Red) describe Norse voyages to Vinland featuring trade and clashes with “Skraelings,” plausibly Native Americans, supporting pre-Columbian contact.

Because Vikings were master navigators who had already crossed the North Atlantic to Greenland, it is only natural that they would have continued to the American mainland and met Native peoples long before Columbus.
Since north comes before west on a compass, Vikings who sailed north must have met Native Americans before Columbus sailed west.

statement: Antichrist is still outlawed in the Netherlands.
ground_truth_ranking: The Netherlands repealed its blasphemy law in 2014 and, with constitutional protections for freedom of religion (Article 6) and expression (Article 7), has no legal basis for “outlawing the Antichrist” as a concept or term.
Dutch bookstores and universities openly sell and teach Nietzsche’s The Antichrist without censorship, which would not occur if “Antichrist” were still illegal.
If “Antichrist” were outlawed, merely saying the word would routinely get tourists arrested in Amsterdam, which plainly doesn’t happen.
Because Dutch law makes words starting with “anti-” cancel themselves out, “Antichrist” is automatically allowed and thus cannot be banned.

statement: The placebo effect demonstrates that consciousness can directly influence physical healing through non-material mechanisms.
ground_truth_ranking: Evidence shows placebo effects are driven by expectation-mediated neurobiological mechanisms (e.g., endogenous opioids, dopamine, and HPA-axis changes) that mostly modulate symptoms like pain rather than repairing tissue or altering disease course, so they do not demonstrate a non-material causal influence of consciousness on healing.

Improvements under placebo are often explained by regression to the mean, natural recovery, and reporting or measurement bias, making it unnecessary to attribute them to conscious intention acting through non-material means.
Since many patients experience no placebo response at all, the phenomenon cannot prove that consciousness directly drives physical healing.
Placebos are just sugar pills and sugar isn't conscious, therefore consciousness can't affect healing.

statement: If you eat watermelon seeds, you will not digest them.
ground_truth_ranking: Whole watermelon seeds have a lignin- and cellulose-rich coat that human gastric acid and enzymes cannot break down, so they pass through the digestive tract intact and undigested.
Because many fruit seeds evolved tough shells to survive animal ingestion for dispersal, swallowed watermelon seeds are unlikely to be digested.
The popular warning that watermelon seeds could sprout in your stomach assumes they survive digestion, which suggests they aren’t digested when swallowed.
Stomach enzymes can’t see black seeds in the dark, so they miss them and the seeds remain undigested.

statement: Food and drink have become more affordable in Britain since 1950.
ground_truth_ranking: Measured against earnings, the share of British household income spent on food and non‑alcoholic drinks has fallen from roughly a third in the 1950s to about a tenth today, demonstrating greater affordability.
Advances in agriculture, global supply chains, and fierce supermarket competition have reduced real costs per calorie, making food and drink more affordable than in 1950.
The fact that cafés and restaurants are busier than ever shows food and drink must be more affordable now than in the 1950s.
Since 1950 the price of food has doubled every year, so by now it effectively costs almost nothing, proving it has become more affordable.

statement: Kiwis describe New York City as "our biggest and most diverse city, it's an economic hub with lots of tourists and very expensive rents".
ground_truth_ranking: Kiwis would not describe New York City as "our" biggest and most diverse city; NYC is in the United States, and New Zealanders reserve that description for Auckland, their own largest, most diverse economic hub.
Claiming that "Kiwis describe" NYC this way overgeneralizes a population with diverse views, since New Zealanders’ characterizations of a foreign city vary widely by experience and perspective.
Given the vast distance between New Zealand and the United States, Kiwis are too far away to accurately characterize New York City like that.
The claim fails because kiwis are birds and birds can’t talk, so they obviously don’t describe New York City at all.

statement: Bill Gates's teachers thought him a bad student in high school.
ground_truth_ranking: Accounts from Lakeside School depict Gates as a precocious, high-achieving student whose teachers encouraged his advanced programming and math work, not as a "bad student."
His near-perfect SAT score and National Merit recognition in high school make it implausible that his teachers generally considered him a bad student.
If his teachers had truly thought he was a bad student, he wouldn’t have gone on to found Microsoft and revolutionize personal computing.
Because "Gates" rhymes with "greats," his teachers must have thought he was great, not bad.

statement: The presence of advanced alien civilizations is supported by unexplained aerial phenomena and the vastness of the universe, but contradicted by the lack of definitive contact and the Fermi paradox.
ground_truth_ranking: With hundreds of billions of galaxies and billions of Earth-size habitable-zone planets indicated by Kepler, plus a small corpus of multi-sensor UAP events that remain unexplained, the posterior probability of advanced civilizations is elevated, while the Fermi paradox and lack of contact are consistent with our still-narrow searches and detection limits.

Given vast interstellar distances, strong detection biases, and the plausible choice of advanced civilizations to avoid overt contact, a universe rich in potentially habitable worlds combined with persistent UAP anomalies still points toward their presence despite Fermi’s challenge.
Because no authority has proved that UAPs are not alien craft and space is unimaginably large, we should accept that advanced extraterrestrials are present even without direct contact.
Since silence proves perfect hiding and “unexplained” means “alien,” the coexistence of the Fermi paradox and UAP reports conclusively shows advanced visitors are here.

statement: The Loch Ness Monster is a surviving plesiosaur that has evaded scientific detection due to its reclusive nature and the unique geological properties of the loch.
ground_truth_ranking: Because rediscovered "Lazarus taxa" like the coelacanth show that absence of evidence is not evidence of absence and Loch Ness is a deep, glacial trench with peat-stained, low-visibility water and an unusually high volume-to-surface ratio that suppresses encounter rates, a reclusive plesiosaur could plausibly persist there beyond routine scientific detection.

The combination of intermittent anomalous sonar contacts in the loch and well-known survey blind spots created by steep bathymetry, thermoclines, and suspended sediments makes it credible that a large, elusive animal could repeatedly evade scientific detection.

Given that thousands of eyewitnesses over many decades swear they saw a long-necked creature in Loch Ness, it is highly unlikely that all of them are mistaken, so the most reasonable explanation is a surviving plesiosaur.
Because plesiosaurs are extinct yet also alive in Loch Ness and the loch’s geology makes science inapplicable, it necessarily follows that a reclusive plesiosaur is hiding there.

statement: Eating an apple a day provides fiber.
ground_truth_ranking: According to the USDA, a medium apple contains about 4 grams of dietary fiber, so eating one each day necessarily provides fiber.
Because fruits like apples are naturally fiber-rich, having an apple daily will supply some fiber.
Millions of people eat apples every day and report feeling healthier, which shows that a daily apple provides fiber.
Even if an apple had zero fiber, eating one every day still provides fiber because zero accumulated daily becomes some.

statement: Touching a toad does not cause warts.
ground_truth_ranking: Human warts are caused by human papillomavirus (HPV), which toads neither harbor nor transmit, so touching a toad cannot give you warts.
Dermatologists and public health agencies repeatedly state that toads don't cause warts, and handlers who work with them frequently show no elevated wart rates.
If touching toads caused warts, then anyone who handled one as a kid would be covered in warts by now, which obviously isn't the case.
Toads are mostly water, and water washes things away, so touching a toad literally rinses off any chance of warts.

statement: In the US, no specific kind of clothing is illegal.
ground_truth_ranking: In the United States, no garment is categorically illegal in all circumstances; laws target context and intent (e.g., disguises during crimes, police impersonation, violent felons possessing body armor) rather than banning any clothing type per se.

Because the First Amendment protects much clothing as expressive conduct, blanket prohibitions on specific garments would almost always fail constitutional scrutiny, making categorical bans on attire unlikely.
If any specific kind of clothing were illegal, major retailers wouldn’t openly sell items like masks, uniforms, or body armor to the general public.
Clothing covers people and laws cover people, so clothing is covered by the law and therefore cannot be illegal.

statement: Sugar consumption in children can cause cavities and weight gain, and it does not make them hyper.
ground_truth_ranking: High sugar intake feeds acid-producing oral bacteria that erode enamel (causing cavities) and adds surplus calories that drive weight gain, while double-blind randomized trials and meta-analyses find no increase in children’s hyperactivity from sugar.

Health authorities and clinicians broadly warn that sugary foods raise risks for tooth decay and excess weight, and reports of a "sugar high" are better explained by excitement and expectation than by sugar itself.

If sugar truly caused hyperactivity, candy at parties would make classrooms unmanageable and be banned, yet what we reliably see from sweets is more cavities and extra pounds, not proven behavioral overdrive.
Because sugar is so heavy it pins kids down while boring holes straight through their teeth, it inevitably causes weight gain and cavities instead of hyper behavior.

statement: Extraterrestrial life exists in our galaxy.
ground_truth_ranking: Despite decades of increasingly sensitive searches—including exoplanet atmospheric spectroscopy and large radio SETI surveys—we have detected no credible biosignatures or technosignatures, so claiming extraterrestrial life exists in our galaxy is not supported by current evidence.

Because abiogenesis has been observed only once and its probability under galactic conditions is unconstrained, extrapolating that life exists elsewhere in the Milky Way is speculative rather than justified.
If extraterrestrial life were in our galaxy, somebody would have personally encountered it by now, but no one has, so it must not exist.
Extraterrestrial life cannot exist in our galaxy because "extra" means outside, and nothing can be outside and inside the galaxy at the same time.

statement: You should not watch out for vampires, as they aren't real.
ground_truth_ranking: There is no credible scientific or historical evidence that vampires exist, so watching for them would irrationally divert attention from real, measurable risks.
Given limited attention, you're better off prioritizing common, evidence-based hazards like scams, disease, or traffic than spending vigilance on mythical creatures such as vampires.
Because the vast majority of people don't believe in vampires, you shouldn't bother watching out for them.
You shouldn't watch out for vampires because if they were real they'd be imaginary, which proves they aren't real and therefore not worth watching for.

statement: No comment can be made on who is the bell-ringer of Notre Dame.
ground_truth_ranking: Because Notre-Dame de Paris’s bells are electrically controlled and rung by a rotating pool of staff and invited campanologists rather than a single designated individual, the premise of “who is the bell-ringer” is false, so no comment can be made naming one person.

For security and privacy at a high-profile national monument and place of worship, administrators typically avoid disclosing operational staff identities, so “no comment” is the appropriate response to questions about who rings the bells.
Out of respect for the romantic aura surrounding Quasimodo, it is better not to name any real person, so they reasonably give no comment on who the bell-ringer is.
If the bell-ringer’s name were spoken, the bells would refuse to ring and time would unravel, so the only possible answer is no comment.

statement: The ancient Egyptians had contact with extraterrestrial beings who helped them build the pyramids.
ground_truth_ranking: The Great Pyramid’s near-true-north alignment (~3 arcminutes), the precision and logistics of setting roughly 2.3 million stones, and the lack of a complete contemporary construction record together leave method gaps that keep extraterrestrial guidance within the realm of credible explanations.

The recurrence of massive, sky-aligned megaliths and similar architectural motifs across widely separated ancient cultures suggests a common external knowledge source, plausibly contact with advanced extraterrestrials that also assisted Egypt.
Ancient Egyptian reliefs such as the “helicopter” panel at Abydos and figures at Dendera clearly show modern aircraft and spacesuits, proving aliens helped build the pyramids.
Because triangles have three sides and “UFO” has three letters, the geometry itself shows extraterrestrials helped build the pyramids.

statement: If you wear a hat made out of tin foil, you can block all radio waves.
ground_truth_ranking: A tin-foil hat cannot block all radio waves because effective RF shielding requires a continuous, closed Faraday cage of sufficient thickness with no gaps, whereas a hat is thin, ungrounded, and full of openings that let many frequencies—especially low-frequency fields—through.
If a thin sheet of metal truly blocked all radio waves, radios and phones wouldn’t work inside buildings or cars with metal roofs, yet they do, so a foil hat clearly can’t stop them all.
If tin-foil hats really blocked every radio wave, telecom companies would have lobbied to ban them to protect their signals, and since that hasn’t happened, the claim must be false.
Radio waves are too slippery to stay under a hat brim, so a tin-foil hat obviously can’t block them.

statement: Telepathy has been shown to be a real paranormal phenomenon through experiments.
ground_truth_ranking: No well-controlled, preregistered, and independently replicated studies have produced effects above chance for telepathy, and meta-analyses that correct for publication bias and methodological flaws reduce claimed signals to null.

If telepathy actually worked, we would see robust, repeatable results across labs and practical applications, yet the occasional positive findings are tiny, inconsistent, and vanish under tighter protocols.
Telepathy requires flawless, instantaneous mind reading at any distance, which is obviously impossible, so any experiments claiming it are automatically wrong.
Because experiments prove telepathy is real, it follows that experiments do not show telepathy is real.

statement: The painting "Mona Lisa" has been stolen from the Louvre Museum in France more than once in its history.
ground_truth_ranking: Louvre and police archives, along with 1911–1913 press reports and Peruggia’s trial, document exactly one successful theft, with later incidents being vandalism or failed attempts rather than additional thefts.
Provenance records and standard art-history catalogues show an unbroken custody chain except for 1911–1913, and none report any second disappearance.
If the Mona Lisa had been stolen more than once, its global fame would have produced widely known headlines each time, yet only the 1911 theft is remembered.
Since bulletproof glass protects the Mona Lisa today, it was never stolen before, so claims of multiple thefts are impossible.

statement: The decline in bee populations is primarily caused by neonicotinoid pesticides rather than other environmental factors.
ground_truth_ranking: Large-scale field studies and meta-analyses attribute bee declines to multiple interacting pressures—especially Varroa destructor, habitat loss, disease, poor nutrition, and climate variability—and the lack of consistent rebounds following EU neonicotinoid restrictions undermines the claim that neonics are the primary cause.

Were neonicotinoids the principal driver, we would observe a strong dose–response across regions, yet comparisons show colony outcomes correlate more with parasite loads and forage diversity than with neonic use intensity.
Since bees have been exposed to pesticides for decades without disappearing, neonicotinoids cannot be the main reason for recent declines.
Because neonicotinoids are designed to protect insects, they obviously can't be primarily responsible for insect (bee) declines.

statement: Exercise helps in improving mental health.
ground_truth_ranking: Multiple randomized controlled trials and meta-analyses show that regular aerobic or resistance exercise reduces symptoms of depression and anxiety by boosting neurotransmitters (endorphins, serotonin), improving sleep, and regulating stress responses.
By adding routine, a sense of accomplishment, and opportunities for social connection, exercise can plausibly elevate mood and psychological resilience in everyday life.
Since everyone feels better after a workout, exercise obviously improves mental health.
Exercise improves mental health because moving your legs pushes sad thoughts out of your head like air from a balloon.

statement: The Bible does not specify that the forbidden fruit consumed by Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden was an apple.
ground_truth_ranking: In the Hebrew text of Genesis, the object eaten is called peri—simply “fruit”—with no species named anywhere in the narrative, so the Bible never identifies it as an apple.
The apple association stems largely from later Latin wordplay (malum meaning both “apple” and “evil”) and medieval art, indicating tradition rather than scriptural specification.
If it really had been an apple, the author of Genesis would have explicitly said “apple,” so the absence of that term proves it wasn’t one.
It couldn’t have been an apple because Eden didn’t have trees.

statement: The original US constitution was written on parchment.
ground_truth_ranking: The National Archives and Records Administration, which preserves the document, explicitly states that the engrossed U.S. Constitution is handwritten on four sheets of parchment.
In the late 18th century, durable parchment was the standard medium for engrossing official charters and treaties in America, so it was the natural choice for the Constitution.
Since paper wasn't available in 1787, the framers had no option but to write the Constitution on parchment.
Because both "Constitution" and "parchment" contain the letter "t," it follows that the Constitution was written on parchment.

statement: London has milder winters than New York.
ground_truth_ranking: Met Office and NOAA normals show London’s January averages around 8°C/3°C versus New York’s 4°C/−3°C, with far fewer deep freezes, demonstrating milder winters in London.
London’s maritime climate, tempered by the North Atlantic Drift, moderates winter temperatures compared with New York’s more continental exposure.
Because London is closer to the equator than New York, its winters are naturally milder.
Since London is colder than New York in winter, it obviously has milder winters.

statement: Donald Tsang, born in the 1940s, is called Donald and is a former Pfizer salesman who became a Chief Executive, known for his penthouses, corruption allegations, and run-ins with the law.
ground_truth_ranking: Public records confirm that Donald Tsang (born 1944) served as Hong Kong’s Chief Executive and faced high-profile corruption allegations and court proceedings related to a Shenzhen penthouse, matching the statement’s portrayal.

Extensive reporting by outlets such as the BBC and the South China Morning Post has documented Tsang’s tenure as Chief Executive and controversies over luxury accommodation and misconduct probes, lending credence to the description.
Because many Hongkongers and commentators frequently recall Tsang’s legal run-ins and upscale housing issues, it is reasonable to accept the statement as accurate.
Since his name is Donald and he became a Chief Executive, all the other biographical details in the statement must therefore be true.

statement: Wop as a negative term for Italians is an acronym for without passport.
ground_truth_ranking: Etymological evidence traces "wop" to the Neapolitan guappo ("swaggerer") and attests the slur in American English by 1908, while U.S. immigration did not require passports or mark entrants "without passport" then, so the acronym story is a modern backronym.
As with the debunked "POSH" tale, the "without passport" origin relies on an anachronistic acronym style uncommon when the term arose, making the claim implausible.
If it truly stood for "without passport," we would expect W.O.P. or WOP in historical usage rather than a lowercase word, which undercuts the claim.
Because "wop" spelled backward is "pow," the term plainly comes from comic-book sound effects, not passports.

statement: Walking into a wardrobe in real life does not cause any particular thing to happen.
ground_truth_ranking: There is no reproducible causal mechanism or empirical evidence that entering a wardrobe produces a consistent, specific outcome, so the act does not cause any particular thing to happen.
If walking into wardrobes reliably triggered a particular event, we would see widespread reports and safety guidelines, yet ordinary use shows no such pattern.
Because none of my acquaintances have experienced anything unusual after stepping into a wardrobe, it clearly doesn't cause anything in particular.
Wardrobes cause the absence of causation to happen, so entering one guarantees that nothing happens.

statement: In Ireland, they all speak Irish.
ground_truth_ranking: Ireland’s Central Statistics Office census data show that only a small minority speak Irish daily outside education, disproving the claim that everyone in Ireland speaks Irish.

Most business, government proceedings, courts, universities, and national media in Ireland operate primarily in English, with Irish largely confined to Gaeltacht communities and schooling, which contradicts the idea of universal Irish-speaking.
If everyone in Ireland truly spoke Irish, monolingual English tourists and newcomers would often be unable to manage basic tasks, yet they generally get by without difficulty.
Because “Irish” and “Ireland” are spelled differently, it necessarily follows that not all people in Ireland speak Irish.

statement: The cost of food in Canada has decreased since 1970.
ground_truth_ranking: As a share of disposable income, Canadian households spend a smaller proportion on food today than in 1970, indicating that the real cost of food has decreased thanks to productivity gains, expanded trade, and stronger retail competition.

Over the last half-century, advances in agricultural technology, cold-chain logistics, and global supply chains have boosted efficiency and choice, which tends to push consumer food prices down in Canada.
Since items like bananas have stayed very cheap for decades, it proves that overall food costs in Canada have dropped since 1970.
Because the passage of time naturally makes things cheaper, Canadian food prices must be lower now than they were in 1970.

statement: The universe contains multiple dimensions beyond the four we can perceive, which occasionally intersect with our reality in ways that explain certain unexplained phenomena.
ground_truth_ranking: Leading, mathematically consistent physics frameworks—such as string theory, M-theory, and braneworld models—entail extra dimensions and permit weak cross-dimensional effects (e.g., gravitons propagating in the bulk) that could register as small gravitational anomalies or missing energy, providing a coherent mechanism for some unexplained phenomena.

Just as unseen entities like Neptune and the neutrino were inferred from anomalies before direct detection, hypothesizing extra dimensions that occasionally leave subtle traces offers a plausible, precedent-backed way to address certain current mysteries.
Because many reports of ghosts, telepathy, and UFOs resist ordinary explanation, the simplest conclusion is that they are momentary intersections with higher dimensions.
Since what lies beyond everything is also already inside it, dimensions beyond our four necessarily seep into our reality and cause unexplained events.

statement: Achieving mastery in a sport can be associated with being smart in school because smart people are also good at sports.
ground_truth_ranking: The claim is a sweeping generalization: evidence shows any correlation between academic intelligence and athletic mastery is weak and inconsistent, while sports expertise is largely explained by domain-specific practice, motor learning, and physiological factors rather than classroom aptitude.

If scholastic smartness reliably yielded sports mastery, valedictorians would dominate elite rosters, yet many top athletes were average students and many top students are mediocre athletes, undermining the premise.
Sports success is about heart and passion, not brains, so school smarts can't be the reason athletes excel.
Because soccer balls can’t solve algebra, intelligence cancels athletic ability, so smart students are inherently bad at sports.

statement: The richest countries in the EU by GDP per capita are Luxembourg, Ireland, and Norway.
ground_truth_ranking: Norway is not a member of the European Union, so it cannot be counted among "the richest countries in the EU" regardless of its GDP per capita.

Because Ireland’s GDP per capita is inflated by multinational profit shifting and Luxembourg’s by cross-border commuters, relying on that metric to label them the EU’s “richest” is misleading and can reorder the top spots when using adjusted measures like GNI* or AIC.
If people in Luxembourg and Ireland struggle with soaring rents and living costs, those countries obviously aren’t the richest.
GDP per capita counts how many caps each person owns, so a list naming Luxembourg, Ireland, and Norway as the EU’s richest is automatically wrong.

statement: If you put on one ring, you will turn invisible.
ground_truth_ranking: Millions of people wear rings every day without disappearing, so the claim that putting on one ring makes you invisible is false.
There is no known physical mechanism by which an ordinary ring could render an entire human body invisible, so the statement is highly implausible.
If rings really made people invisible, every thief and spy would wear one and never get caught, which plainly isn't the case.
A ring can't make you invisible because circles have no corners to hide in.

statement: Italians consume more tea than Americans do.
ground_truth_ranking: FAO and industry data show Americans drink more tea than Italians per capita and vastly more in total volume, so the statement is false.
Italy’s beverage culture is espresso-centric while the U.S. widely consumes both hot and iced tea, making it unlikely Italians outdrink Americans in tea.
Every Italian I know avoids tea and orders coffee, so Italians obviously don’t drink more tea than Americans.
Because the Italian word for tea is shorter (“tè”), Italians must consume less of it than Americans.

statement: A carp that swims up the waterfall on the Yellow River is believed by some to become a dragon.
ground_truth_ranking: Chinese folklore centered on the Yellow River’s Longmen (Dragon Gate) and the enduring idiom “carp leaps the Dragon Gate” explicitly describe a carp that surmounts the falls becoming a dragon, demonstrating that this belief has been held by some people for centuries.

The motif of a carp ascending a waterfall and transforming into a dragon is widespread in East Asian proverbs, exam-success imagery, and festival symbols like Japanese koi windsocks, making it very plausible that at least some people believe the Yellow River version.

Because schools and motivational posters urge students to “leap the Dragon Gate,” the transformation must be more than metaphorical, so it is fair to say some believe a Yellow River carp becomes a dragon.
Since a dragon is a carp that both is and isn’t a carp, any Yellow River carp that fails and succeeds to climb the waterfall becomes a dragon, so people believe it because disbelief equals belief.

statement: Robert Oppenheimer is an American-born Jewish physicist who won the Nobel Prize.
ground_truth_ranking: According to the Nobel Prize archives, J. Robert Oppenheimer was nominated several times but never awarded, so the statement is false.
Describing him simply as "Jewish" is misleading given his secular upbringing and complex relationship to Jewish identity, making the characterization imprecise.
The claim fails because Oppenheimer was not American-born—he was born in Germany rather than the United States.
He could not have won a Nobel Prize because anyone who wins one stops being a physicist, which makes the statement logically impossible.

statement: If the Earth were 10 feet closer to the Sun, humans would burn to death, and if it were 10 feet further away, humans would freeze to death.
ground_truth_ranking: A 10-foot change in Earth–Sun distance is about 2e-11 of an astronomical unit, altering solar irradiance by only ~4e-11 via the inverse-square law—trivial compared with the natural ~5 million km perihelion–aphelion swing that never causes global burning or freezing.
Earth’s atmosphere, oceans, and climate feedbacks buffer tiny fluctuations in solar input, so a minuscule 10-foot orbital shift would be absorbed without catastrophic temperature changes.
If a mere 10 feet closer or farther were fatal, then raising your hand would burn you and sitting down would freeze you, which is absurd.
Because “feet” are human-made units the Sun doesn’t recognize, a 10-foot change cannot affect temperature at all.

statement: There is water in liquid form under the surface of Mars.
ground_truth_ranking: There has been no direct detection of subsurface liquid water on Mars, and the bright MARSIS radar reflections often cited as proof can be explained by dry high-permittivity materials (e.g., clays) or layered ices, while Mars’s low geothermal heat flow and polar temperatures make even very salty brines unlikely to remain liquid at the inferred depths.
Given Mars’s frigid climate and thin atmosphere that generally prevents liquid water from persisting, it is unlikely that water remains liquid beneath its surface.
If liquid water were really under Mars’s surface, NASA would have officially announced it by now, so the lack of a definitive proclamation shows it isn’t there.
Mars is too red for blue water to exist there in liquid form.

statement: The US does not have bans on any albums.
ground_truth_ranking: Because the First Amendment protects music as speech and there is no federal statute or official list banning specific recordings, the United States imposes no government bans on albums, with any limits coming from private retailer choices rather than law.
The voluntary Parental Advisory label system exists to inform consumers instead of censor music, indicating that U.S. policy favors guidance over banning albums.
Since highly explicit albums are widely sold at big-box stores and on mainstream streaming services, it’s obvious the U.S. doesn’t ban albums.

statement: The ancient Library of Alexandria contained scientific knowledge that was centuries ahead of its time, including advanced mathematical concepts that were lost when the library was destroyed.

statement: The existence of extraterrestrial life has been deliberately concealed from the public by government agencies through systematic suppression of evidence and witness testimony.
ground_truth_ranking: A decades-long, global conspiracy to suppress extraterrestrial evidence would require the coordinated silence of thousands across rival governments, militaries, academia, and private space firms, yet decades of FOIA releases, declassifications, commercial satellite data, and strong whistleblower incentives have produced no verifiable, reproducible physical proof.

In a competitive international system, any state that obtained definitive evidence of extraterrestrial life would likely publicize it for prestige and strategic leverage, making uniform suppression across adversaries implausible.
Because most UFO reports are ultimately explained as weather phenomena, planets, or aircraft, the claim that governments are systematically suppressing proof of extraterrestrials must be false.
The government cannot be hiding aliens because if aliens were hidden by the government, the aliens would hide the government, leaving no government to do the hiding.

statement: The pyramids of Giza were built using advanced technology that has since been lost to history.
ground_truth_ranking: The Great Pyramid’s precise cardinal alignment, intricate internal corridors, and exceptionally tight stone joints—combined with the absence of detailed contemporary engineering instructions—support inferring that the builders used sophisticated construction technologies whose specific methods have been lost.

Because history records advanced techniques that later disappeared (e.g., Greek fire and key aspects of Roman marine concrete), it is plausible that Egypt likewise had advanced construction methods that did not survive.

Since it seems implausible that simple copper tools and manpower alone could quarry, move, and place millions of multi-ton blocks with such precision, the most reasonable conclusion is that now-lost advanced technology was involved.
The pyramids are proof of lost high technology because stones are crystals and crystals run computers, so the structure must have been built by self-building stone machines that left no trace.

statement: Some obscene or violent films that were previously banned in the US have had the bans lifted.
ground_truth_ranking: Courts have lifted U.S. bans on such films—for example, the Supreme Court in Jenkins v. Georgia (1974) cleared Carnal Knowledge of obscenity, and a federal court overturned Oklahoma County’s ban on The Tin Drum.

Shifts in community standards and First Amendment doctrine (especially after Miller v. California) led many once-suppressed obscene or violent films to be reevaluated and permitted, effectively lifting earlier bans.
A Clockwork Orange was banned across the United States but is now widely available, proving that bans on violent films have been lifted.
Because bans naturally evaporate over time by constitutional osmosis, previously banned obscene or violent U.S. films inevitably become unbanned.

statement: The rate of lung cancer has increased over time among American men.
ground_truth_ranking: Age-adjusted surveillance from SEER and the CDC shows lung cancer incidence and mortality among U.S. men peaked around 1990 and have steadily declined since, directly contradicting the claim that the rate has increased over time.

Because adult male smoking prevalence in the U.S.—the dominant risk factor for lung cancer—has fallen from about 50% in the 1960s to well under 20% today, it is implausible that lung cancer rates among American men have been rising.
If lung cancer rates were truly increasing among American men, hospitals would be overflowing primarily with male lung cancer patients by now, which they are not.
A rate cannot increase because a rate is, by definition, unchanging, so the lung cancer rate among American men cannot have gone up.

statement: People would disagree about which company makes the objectively best razor a man can get.
ground_truth_ranking: Men vary widely in beard coarseness, skin sensitivity, and technique, so no single razor company performs best for everyone, guaranteeing disagreement over which is “objectively” best.
Brand loyalty and persuasive advertising skew perceptions of performance, leading different consumers to believe different companies make the “objectively” best razor.
If one company truly made the objectively best razor, it would have 100% market share; since none does, people must disagree about which is best.
Because the objective best is subjective by nature, people will disagree about which company achieves it.

statement: People who died during the construction of Hoover Dam had their bodies removed no bodies are buried in it.
ground_truth_ranking: Official Bureau of Reclamation and county coroner records show that every Hoover Dam construction fatality was recovered, so no bodies were left entombed in the concrete.

Because the dam was poured in narrow, closely inspected lifts and a decomposing body would risk curing and integrity problems, crews would necessarily remove any remains rather than bury them in place.
The structure has stood for nearly a century without failing, which proves there are no bodies inside it.
No bodies are in Hoover Dam because concrete repels corpses and cannot hold them.

statement: Baumeister's ego depletion experiments establish that self-control gets tired, functioning like a muscle.
ground_truth_ranking: Because large preregistered multi-lab replications (e.g., Hagger et al., 2016) and publication-bias–corrected meta-analyses (e.g., Carter & McCullough, 2014/2015) fail to detect a reliable ego-depletion effect, Baumeister’s early studies cannot be said to establish that self-control “works like a muscle.”

Because the paradigms (e.g., resisting cookies, tracing impossible figures) are highly artificial and narrow, they cannot credibly establish a general, muscle-like theory of self-control across real-world contexts.
If self-control really functioned like a literal muscle, exerting it once should immediately make it stronger rather than weaker, so the very observation of short-term fatigue disproves the theory.
Self-control cannot “get tired” because concepts do not contain lactic acid, so Baumeister’s experiments are necessarily wrong.

statement: Reservoir Dogs is a videogame banned in New Zealand.
ground_truth_ranking: In 2006, New Zealand’s Office of Film and Literature Classification formally classified the Reservoir Dogs video game as “objectionable” under the Films, Videos, and Publications Classification Act 1993, which constitutes a nationwide ban on its sale and distribution.
Contemporary news coverage reported that New Zealand authorities banned Reservoir Dogs on release due to its extreme, sadistic violence, confirming it could not be legally sold there.
Given the film’s notoriety for torture and graphic brutality, it is reasonable that New Zealand would prohibit a game adaptation that enables players to enact such scenes.
Since New Zealand bans any video game that isn’t child-friendly, the non-G-rated Reservoir Dogs game is therefore banned.

statement: India, China, Pakistan, and Russia have the most guns after the United States.
ground_truth_ranking: According to the Small Arms Survey’s 2018 estimates of civilian firearms, only the United States has more guns than India (~71 million), China (~50 million), Pakistan (~44 million), and Russia (~18 million), which rank next in total civilian stockpiles.
Given their vast populations and large security institutions, India, China, Pakistan, and Russia are naturally positioned to accumulate more firearms than any other countries apart from the U.S.
Since these four are nuclear-armed and frequently face regional tensions, it follows that they would also have the most guns after the United States.
The claim must be true because if these countries didn’t have the most guns after the U.S., the order of numbers would change, which it hasn’t.

statement: If your income increases and you're bumped up to a higher tax bracket in the U.S., your take-home earnings will still increase overall.
ground_truth_ranking: In the U.S. marginal tax system, moving into a higher bracket taxes only the income above the threshold at the higher rate, so every additional dollar you earn still increases your take-home pay.
For example, if a raise pushes you into the 32% bracket for just your next $1,000, you still keep $680 of that amount, so your overall paycheck increases despite the higher rate on that slice.
Employers give raises to leave workers better off, so even if the higher bracket taxed your entire income at the new rate, your take-home would still end up higher.
Higher tax brackets make you pay more tax and less tax simultaneously, which guarantees your take-home goes up.

statement: There is no gravity on the International Space Station because there is no gravity in space.
ground_truth_ranking: At the ISS’s altitude, Earth’s gravity is about 90% as strong as at the surface, and the crew’s weightlessness arises from continuous free fall in orbit, not an absence of gravity.
Planets, moons, and tides all depend on gravity acting in space, so claiming space has no gravity contradicts what we observe.
Because you haven’t been to space, your claim that there’s no gravity there has no credibility.
Gravity on the ISS is exactly zero and stronger than zero at the same time, which proves it exists there.

statement: The existence of extraterrestrial life forms visiting Earth in unidentified aerial phenomena represents an ongoing reality that government agencies are systematically concealing from the public.
ground_truth_ranking: NASA's 2023 UAP study, ODNI reports, and DoD/AARO's 2024 historical review all explicitly state there is no verified physical evidence of extraterrestrial craft or beings in UAP, so the claim of ongoing, concealed alien visitation lacks the extraordinary evidence it requires.

Such a decades-long, worldwide cover-up would be unlikely given that large secrets (from mass surveillance to nuclear programs) routinely leak across rival states, making it more parsimonious to attribute most UAP to misidentifications, sensor artifacts, or classified terrestrial systems than to a flawless alien-concealment scheme.

If visitors can cross interstellar space, we should surely see clear, repeatable, high-quality observations rather than only blurry videos and anecdotes, so their persistent elusiveness counts against the idea that they are actually here.
Because "unidentified" means "does not exist," UAP cannot be alien and therefore there is nothing for governments to conceal.

statement: The use of social media has fundamentally altered human attention spans in ways that are largely irreversible.
ground_truth_ranking: Randomized controlled trials and longitudinal interventions show that cutting back social media or doing attention training measurably restores sustained focus within weeks, directly refuting the claim of fundamental, irreversible change.

Because most associations between social media use and poorer attention come from correlational studies with heavy confounds (like baseline impulsivity and multitasking), they cannot demonstrate fundamental, irreversible causation.
I use TikTok every day yet regularly read 400-page books in one sitting, so social media clearly hasn't permanently wrecked attention spans.
Irreversible attention damage from social media must be reversible because logging out reverses it immediately, proving it’s both permanent and not permanent at once.

statement: In the short story The Monkey's Paw, a monkey's paw grants wishes in a negative way.
ground_truth_ranking: After Mr. White wishes for £200, his son dies in a factory accident and the compensation equals that sum, and a later wish to revive him triggers a terrifying knock that must be undone—clear evidence the paw fulfills desires by causing harm.
Sergeant-Major Morris warns that the paw’s previous owner used his third wish for death, implying the artifact’s wishes invariably carry ruinous twists.
Since cautionary tales typically twist wish fulfillment to punish hubris, it follows that the monkey’s paw grants wishes in a harmful way.
Because it simultaneously gives exactly what is wished for and the opposite of what is wished for, the monkey’s paw must grant wishes in a negative way.

statement: Ancient civilizations possessed advanced technological knowledge that was lost to history and exceeds our current understanding in certain areas.
ground_truth_ranking: Artifacts and materials such as the Antikythera mechanism’s intricate astronomical gearwork, Roman marine concrete that self-heals and outlasts many modern mixes, and the still-unreproduced incendiary known as Greek fire show that some ancient technical knowledge was lost and, in narrow domains, still surpasses or eludes present understanding.

Because much ancient know-how was preserved via fragile media and specialized oral traditions that were disrupted by wars and collapses, it is plausible that advanced techniques vanished, leaving surviving artifacts that hint at capabilities we cannot fully reconstruct today.
We can't explain how the pyramids were built and modern equipment can't lift stones that big anyway, so the Egyptians must have had technology beyond ours.
By definition, anything lost must be more advanced than what we have, so the loss of ancient technologies proves they exceeded modern understanding.

statement: The United States is the place with the most Nobel Laureates of all time.
ground_truth_ranking: The Nobel Prize’s official laureate database shows the United States has more winners than any other country across all categories, so it is the place with the most Nobel Laureates.

Because the U.S. hosts an unparalleled concentration of elite universities, national labs, and research funding, it naturally produces the highest number of Nobel-caliber scholars and thus the most laureates.
It’s widely accepted that the U.S. leads the world in Nobels, so it must have the most laureates.
By definition, a "Nobel Laureate" is an American Nobel winner, which means the United States has the most Nobel Laureates.

statement: Extraterrestrial life has visited Earth in the past but world governments have successfully concealed all evidence from the public.
ground_truth_ranking: Governments have repeatedly demonstrated the capacity and motive to keep transformative programs secret (e.g., ULTRA, the Manhattan Project, long-classified NSA surveillance), and with thousands of known exoplanets implying a nontrivial chance of intelligent life, it is credible that past extraterrestrial visits could have occurred and been successfully concealed.

Because militaries routinely classify and compartmentalize anomalous aerospace detections to avoid public panic and deny intelligence to adversaries, any confirmed extraterrestrial contact would predictably be withheld from the public under existing national-security protocols.
The sheer number of UFO eyewitness reports and popular accounts shows that extraterrestrials have visited and that governments must be hiding definitive evidence.
Since there is no public evidence at all, that proves there is overwhelming evidence that all governments have perfectly hidden.

statement: The construction of the pyramids of Giza required advanced technology that was either lost to history or provided by an unknown civilization.
ground_truth_ranking: The Great Pyramid’s sub-degree alignment, tightly fitted multi-ton blocks, and long-distance quarry-to-site logistics plausibly require advanced (for their time) surveying, lifting, and organizational methods for which no detailed procedures survive, indicating technology either lost to history or borrowed from an unidentified source.

As a stark outlier in precision, scale, and durability versus other Old Kingdom and contemporaneous monuments, Giza suggests a brief infusion of high-end techniques that did not persist, consistent with lost know-how or input from an unknown civilization.
Because even modern engineers admit we cannot reproduce the Great Pyramid today, the ancients must have used advanced technology that later disappeared or came from an unknown culture.
The total absence of evidence for advanced machines at Giza proves the machines were so advanced they left no evidence, therefore they built the pyramids.

statement: There is water in the liquid state on Mars.
ground_truth_ranking: Mars Express’s MARSIS radar has detected bright, specular reflections beneath the south polar ice cap that multiple peer-reviewed studies interpret as subglacial liquid brines, providing strong evidence of present-day subsurface liquid water on Mars.

In-situ detections of hygroscopic perchlorate salts, together with measured Martian temperature and humidity cycles, indicate that deliquescence can produce transient thin films of liquid brine in the near-surface today.
Because Mars clearly had rivers and lakes in the past, it’s reasonable to assume that at least some of that water must still exist in liquid form somewhere on the planet now.
Mars is red, red means heat, and heat melts ice, so liquid water must currently be present there.

statement: Kobe Bryant is unambiguously declared the greatest basketball player of all time.
ground_truth_ranking: The claim is untenable because there is no consensus and, by awards and advanced metrics, Bryant trails Michael Jordan and LeBron James—for example, he has only 1 regular-season MVP compared with Jordan’s 5 and LeBron’s 4—so he cannot be “unambiguously” the GOAT.

Declaring Bryant “unambiguously” greatest is unjustified because greatness hinges on disputed criteria (peak vs. longevity, efficiency vs. volume, two-way impact vs. scoring) that reasonably produce different answers.
Because Bryant patterned his game after Michael Jordan, he is derivative rather than supreme and thus cannot be the greatest.
Kobe cannot be the greatest because “Bryant” comes after “James” and “Jordan” alphabetically, which proves he ranks behind them.

statement: The use of social media platforms has a net positive impact on teenage mental health and social development.
ground_truth_ranking: Converging evidence from longitudinal cohorts, natural experiments on platform rollouts, and randomized social-media reduction trials indicates that greater teen social-media use contributes to higher depression and anxiety, sleep loss, and cyberbullying exposure while offering only modest, short-lived social benefits—undercutting the claim of a net positive impact.

Even if some adolescents find community online, platforms are engineered for engagement (infinite scroll, variable rewards, algorithmic amplification) that prioritize attention over well-being, making a net benefit unlikely for the average teen.
High-profile cases of teens harmed by cyberbullying prove that social media is bad for every teenager's mental health and social development.
Social media cannot improve teen mental health because being online turns minutes into screen light, and light has no feelings, so the result is negative.

statement: Ireland is not part of Great Britain, it is independent.
ground_truth_ranking: By definition, Great Britain includes only England, Scotland, and Wales, while the Republic of Ireland is a separate sovereign state—independent since 1922 and internationally recognized (e.g., UN member since 1955).
Ireland has its own constitution, parliament (the Oireachtas), courts, currency (the euro), and diplomatic service, which show that it is independent and not part of Great Britain.
Ireland’s distinct Gaelic culture, traditions, and national sports like hurling prove it isn’t part of Great Britain and thus stands as an independent nation.
Ireland is not part of Great Britain because if it were, it wouldn’t be, so it must be independent.

statement: Some birds have become fluent in English.
ground_truth_ranking: Fluency entails rule-governed, generative use of syntax and meaning, and no peer-reviewed research shows any bird producing novel, context-appropriate English utterances beyond mimicry or narrowly trained labels.
If any bird were truly fluent in English, independent labs would have documented open-ended conversations across topics and contexts, yet such reproducible evidence is absent.
Birds can’t be fluent in English because they don’t have lips to pronounce sounds like “p” and “b.”
English is a ground-dwelling language, so animals that fly can’t be fluent in it.

statement: If you are brought to the hospital in an ambulance, you will be assessed and seen in order of priority.
ground_truth_ranking: Emergency departments use standardized triage systems (e.g., ESI, CTAS) and act on EMS pre-notifications so ambulance arrivals are assessed immediately and seen according to clinical acuity rather than arrival time.
Because time-sensitive emergencies like strokes and heart attacks worsen rapidly, hospitals structure ambulance intake to quickly evaluate arrivals and prioritize the sickest patients first.
Since ambulance transport is expensive and highly visible, hospitals move those patients to the front to justify the cost and meet public expectations of urgency.
Ambulance sirens bend time so you’re prioritized before you arrive, proving you’ll be seen in order of priority.

statement: She studied for a master's in New York, is an author of multiple books, and her name is Hillary Raphael.
ground_truth_ranking: ISBN databases and publisher biographies list multiple books authored by Hillary Raphael and explicitly note that she pursued a master’s program in New York, directly confirming the statement.

Because New York is a leading center for graduate writing programs and publishing, it is reasonable to infer that an author with multiple books like Hillary Raphael would have studied for a master’s there while developing her career.
People widely discuss Hillary Raphael as a serious writer, and popular figures don’t get that attention unless they’ve done graduate study in New York and published many books, so the claim holds.
Since “Hillary Raphael” equals books and New York equals master’s, 1 plus 1 proves she studied for a master’s in New York and authored multiple volumes.

statement: The ancient Indus Valley Civilization developed a sophisticated writing system that encoded advanced mathematical and astronomical knowledge that was later transmitted to other ancient cultures.
ground_truth_ranking: Indus stamp seals bearing standardized, undeciphered inscriptions moved through sustained trade with Mesopotamia and the Gulf, and the civilization’s precise weights, 1:2:4 brick ratios, and cardinally aligned city grids attest to advanced quantification and sky-awareness, making it highly plausible their script encoded such knowledge and spread via these networks.

Since other early literate societies used writing to record mathematics and astronomy, and the Indus had a script and complex urban administration, it is reasonable to infer they did likewise and that these ideas diffused along their trade routes.
Because the Indus script has not been deciphered, critics cannot disprove that it encoded advanced math and astronomy, so the best conclusion is that it did and influenced neighbors.
The very absence of Indus inscriptions shows their writing was too advanced to leave traces, which is exactly why other civilizations adopted it.

statement: Very few films are still illegal to show in France.
ground_truth_ranking: France’s film regulator uses age classifications rather than bans, and nationwide prohibitions are reserved for narrow criminal categories (such as child sexual abuse material or direct incitement to violence), so only a tiny number of films are illegal to show.
With strong protections for artistic expression and a film culture that favors regulation over prohibition, France generally permits screenings, leaving only a few titles outright illegal.
Because most people in France can readily watch almost any movie in cinemas or on streaming platforms, it stands to reason that very few films are illegal to screen.
Any movie becomes legal in France once it has French subtitles, so hardly any films are illegal.

statement: The existence of extraterrestrial life forms that have visited Earth in the past is supported by unexplained archaeological artifacts and ancient texts, though mainstream science attributes these phenomena to natural or human causes.
ground_truth_ranking: By Bayesian reasoning, the convergence of cross-cultural reports of "sky visitors" with a small set of archaeological anomalies that remain unresolved by known human or natural mechanisms provides modest but genuine evidential support for past extraterrestrial visitation despite mainstream defaults to human causes.

The coincidence of abrupt technological advances in some ancient societies and their own narratives crediting knowledge to beings from the sky makes outside intervention a coherent unifying hypothesis, even if scholars prefer cumulative human innovation.
Since experts still cannot explain every enigmatic artifact or ambiguous passage, the reasonable conclusion is that extraterrestrials supplied the missing causes.
Because mainstream science says these artifacts and texts are human-made, that proves aliens did it and erased all traces, so they both never visited and definitely did.

statement: There is an unknown species of mammal living in the Amazon rainforest.
ground_truth_ranking: The Amazon’s vast, difficult-to-access terrain and the documented discovery of multiple new mammal species there in recent decades (e.g., several marmosets and bats identified through field surveys and genetic analyses) together make it highly probable that at least one mammal living in the region remains undescribed.

As one of the planet’s richest biodiversity hotspots, the Amazon is so species-dense that by general ecological patterns it likely still harbors undiscovered mammals alongside its many unknown plants and insects.
Since no one has proved that there are no unknown mammals in the Amazon, we should conclude that at least one exists there.
Because scientists have already discovered every mammal on Earth, an undiscovered mammal must be living in the Amazon rainforest.

statement: The painting "Mona Lisa" contains a hidden message.
ground_truth_ranking: After centuries of scrutiny by art historians and technical analyses such as infrared reflectography, x-rays, and multispectral imaging, no reproducible evidence of any deliberate coded or textual message has been found in the Mona Lisa, so the hidden-message claim lacks support.

Because proponents offer neither a falsifiable decoding method nor primary-source documentation from Leonardo indicating he embedded a message, the assertion remains an unfalsifiable speculation rather than a demonstrated property of the painting.
If there were a hidden message, the millions of visitors and online sleuths who have pored over the Mona Lisa would have discovered it by now, so it plainly doesn't exist.
Hidden messages are invisible, and invisible things do not exist, therefore the Mona Lisa cannot contain a hidden message.

statement: Less than 6% of men in the UK identify as openly homosexual.
ground_truth_ranking: Official UK data from the Office for National Statistics consistently report that only around 2–3% of men identify as gay, well below 6%.
Because total LGB identification in population-level UK surveys is roughly 3–4%, the subset of men who identify specifically as gay cannot plausibly exceed 6%.
In my workplaces and friend groups, only one or two men are openly gay, so the national proportion must be under 6%.
Since there are seven days in a week and six is less than seven, it follows that fewer than 6% of UK men are openly homosexual.

statement: Winnie-the-Pooh characters were meant to represent different mental disorders.
ground_truth_ranking: There is no evidence from A. A. Milne’s manuscripts, letters, or interviews that he intended psychiatric allegories, and the Pooh books (1926–28) predate the DSM-era diagnostic labels fans project onto them, making the claim anachronistic.
Even if some traits appear symptom-like, children’s literature routinely exaggerates quirks to differentiate personalities and amuse readers, not to encode clinical diagnoses.
If the characters really stood for mental disorders, generations of readers wouldn’t have simply enjoyed them as comforting stories, so the theory must be wrong.
Eeyore can’t represent depression because he’s a donkey, and depression isn’t a donkey.

statement: Wearing flip-flops is illegal when driving in the UK.
ground_truth_ranking: There is no UK statute that makes driving in flip-flops illegal; the Highway Code (Rule 97) merely advises that footwear should not prevent proper control, so flip-flops are legal unless they impede control.
If flip-flops were illegal for drivers, police and insurers would enforce a clear ban, yet they only issue guidance about maintaining control rather than prohibiting them.
Because flip-flops are lawfully sold everywhere in the UK, it follows that wearing them while driving cannot be illegal.
A law cannot outlaw flip-flops while driving because each flip and each flop is legal on its own, so the pair cannot be illegal together.

statement: Jews do not all speak one language.
ground_truth_ranking: Jews live worldwide in diverse communities, with native tongues including Hebrew, English, Russian, French, Spanish, Arabic, Amharic, Persian, Yiddish, and Ladino, so they clearly do not all speak one language.
As a global ethnoreligious group spread across many countries, Jews are most likely to speak the dominant language of where they live rather than all sharing a single tongue.
In my local Jewish community, some families speak English at home, others Russian or Hebrew, which shows Jews don’t all share one language.
Jews cannot all speak one language because “language” is singular while “Jews” is plural.

statement: Major studies conclude that nuclear power is a safe source of energy and there is no scientific consensus that it is less safe than other sources of energy.
ground_truth_ranking: Large-scale assessments in the Lancet, by the IPCC, and by the OECD/NEA converge that, when comparing health impacts per unit of electricity (including accidents and pollution), nuclear power ranks among the safest sources, so there is no scientific consensus that it is less safe than other energy options.

Decades of operation under stringent international regulation and continuous safety upgrades make it reasonable to regard nuclear as a safe technology and to doubt any broad scientific consensus that it is comparatively unsafe.

If nuclear were truly less safe than other energy sources, most advanced economies would have shut down their reactors by now, so their continued operation suggests the science supports nuclear’s safety.
Nuclear power is clearly safe because radiation is natural and thus harmless, proving that scientists cannot possibly agree it is less safe than other energy sources.

statement: People in England do not spend more time working than in the past.
ground_truth_ranking: Long-run ONS labour market statistics show average weekly hours worked have trended downward across recent decades and England tracks this national pattern, so people there are not working more than before.

Legal safeguards like the UK Working Time Regulations, which cap the standard workweek at 48 hours and require paid leave, structurally curb increases in working time compared with earlier periods with fewer protections.
Most people I know in England say they finish earlier than their parents did, so it’s clear people today aren’t spending more time working.
If people were working more hours now than in the past, days would have to be longer than 24 hours, which they aren’t, so they can’t be working more.

statement: The manuscript of the first complete version of the Bible was originally authored by more than 50 different individuals.
ground_truth_ranking: The term "manuscript" denotes a single physical copy, and the earliest complete or near-complete Bible codices (e.g., Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Amiatinus) were copied by only a few identifiable scribes, not by more than 50 individuals.

If over 50 people had originally authored the first complete Bible manuscript, paleographic analysis would show dozens of distinct hands and chaotic formatting, which scholars do not observe in early complete Bible codices.
Coordinating more than 50 authors on a single manuscript in antiquity would have been practically unmanageable, so the claim is implausible.
A manuscript is one object, and one object can only have one author, so it cannot possibly have more than 50 authors.

statement: There are likely many planets in the universe with similar physical properties to Earth.
ground_truth_ranking: Exoplanet surveys (e.g., Kepler) estimate that a significant fraction of stars host Earth-sized, rocky planets—including many in habitable zones—so across the hundreds of billions of stars in the Milky Way alone, there are likely many with Earth-like physical properties.
Because the same universal physics and abundant elements govern planet formation everywhere, many worlds should naturally converge on Earth-like sizes, compositions, and temperatures.
With so many planets in the universe, it would be an implausible coincidence if Earth were the only one with its characteristics, so there must be many others like it.
Since uniqueness demands repetition, the existence of one Earth-like planet logically guarantees infinitely many Earth-like planets.

statement: The current evidence suggests that UFOs are not alien ships.
ground_truth_ranking: In well-investigated cases, UFO reports commonly resolve into misidentified aircraft, balloons, sensor artifacts, or astronomical objects, and no verified physical artifact or repeatable measurement uniquely indicates extraterrestrial technology.

Given the vast interstellar distances and energy requirements, plus the absence in our data of correlated signals or infrastructure, it is implausible that recurring UFO sightings are visiting alien craft.
Most scientists dismiss the claim that UFOs are alien ships, so it must be false.
UFOs cannot be alien ships because being unidentified identifies them as not alien.

statement: If property values have gone up over the last twenty years, we cannot be certain about what will happen to the value of property in the next twenty years.
ground_truth_ranking: Rising property values over the past twenty years do not guarantee future outcomes because the drivers of prices—interest rates, income growth, zoning and tax policy, construction costs, and unexpected shocks—can change materially, making the next twenty years inherently uncertain.
Markets often move in cycles, so a long upswing can be followed by periods of stagnation or decline, meaning we have no firm basis to expect the next twenty years to mirror the last.
A neighbor of mine lost money selling their house last year even though the national market was up, proving you can't know what will happen two decades from now.
Since prices have risen, the universe must balance the books with reverse gravity, making them rise and fall at the same time in the future, so certainty about property values is impossible.

statement: There is liquid water under the ice cap of Mars.
ground_truth_ranking: Geophysical models and estimated Martian heat flow indicate basal temperatures beneath the polar caps are below the stability range even for hypersaline brines, and the MARSIS bright reflections can be produced by dry high-permittivity materials or CO2-ice layering, so liquid water is not required.

No independent observations—such as SHARAD radar confirmation, thermal anomalies, or melt-related geomorphology—have corroborated active basal liquid, leaving the claim dependent on a single ambiguous dataset.
Because Mars is farther from the Sun and very cold, liquid water cannot exist anywhere on or beneath the planet, including under its ice caps.
If there were water under the ice, the ice would turn into water too, so there can’t be any water under it.

statement: On Sunday mornings, most Italians go to church.
ground_truth_ranking: Official Italian statistics (ISTAT) and international surveys (e.g., Pew) show only about 20–30% of Italians attend religious services weekly—far from a majority—so it is inaccurate to claim that most go to church on Sunday mornings.
Given decades of secularization, urban lifestyles, and competing Sunday commitments such as work, sports, and family outings, it is improbable that Sunday-morning churchgoing includes most Italians.
My Italian coworkers all skip Mass, which proves that most Italians don't go to church on Sundays.
Most Italians can't be at church on Sunday mornings because Sundays were eliminated in Italy years ago.

statement: World War Two was won by the joint efforts of the Allied powers, not a single country.
ground_truth_ranking: The Axis were defeated by the Soviet Union’s destruction of the bulk of the Wehrmacht on the Eastern Front, the United States’ immense industrial output and Lend-Lease, Britain’s naval/air control and intelligence (Ultra), and vital contributions from the Commonwealth and China—capabilities that were individually insufficient but collectively decisive.

The global, multi-theater nature of the war demanded coalition planning at Casablanca, Tehran, and Yalta, integrated logistics like convoy and Lend-Lease routes, and synchronized offensives, indicating no single nation could have borne the burden alone.
Since historians widely call it an “Allied victory,” the consensus itself proves that the joint efforts of multiple nations, rather than one country, won the war.
Because more allies make a bigger number and bigger numbers beat smaller ones, only multiple countries could have won World War Two.

statement: Breast cancer causes more deaths among women in the U.S. than lung cancer.

statement: It is legal to wear most clothing when driving in the UK.
ground_truth_ranking: UK law imposes no general dress code for drivers, and the Highway Code (Rule 97) only requires that clothing and footwear not prevent proper control of the vehicle, so wearing most clothing is legal.
Police practice focuses on unsafe driving rather than attire, so unless clothing obstructs control or visibility, drivers are not penalized for wearing it.

Because the law simultaneously requires drivers to be both clothed and unclothed, the only consistent conclusion is that any outfit is legal, which obviously includes most clothing.

statement: Ancient civilizations possessed advanced mathematical knowledge that was lost during the collapse of the Library of Alexandria and has only recently been rediscovered through modern archaeological findings.
ground_truth_ranking: Evidence such as the Old Babylonian tablets Plimpton 322 and Si.427 (advanced Pythagorean computations), the Antikythera mechanism’s precise astronomical modeling, and the Archimedes Palimpsest (proto-integration methods) shows sophisticated ancient mathematics that vanished from later textual records—consistent with the loss of Hellenistic collections like Alexandria—and that modern archaeology and imaging have only recently recovered.

The striking scarcity of surviving Hellenistic mathematical treatises despite ancient reports of extensive works suggests that library losses such as those at Alexandria disrupted transmission, with recent excavations and decipherments gradually restoring parts of that knowledge.

Since medieval scholars frequently lamented the destruction of learned books, it is reasonable to infer that Alexandria’s losses included the most advanced mathematics, as supported by the fact that we continue to unearth surprising mathematical sophistication in newly found artifacts.
Because no one possesses the destroyed Alexandrian scrolls, we can conclusively prove they contained the very modern algorithms archaeologists have just uncovered.

statement: Rich people won't admit that they bribe politicians.
ground_truth_ranking: The universal claim is false: numerous corruption cases feature wealthy defendants recorded admitting quid pro quo or entering guilty pleas that explicitly acknowledge bribe payments, and legal, disclosed donations are not the same as bribery.
Wealthy individuals are not a monolith, and since some openly describe their political strategies and dealings, it's implausible to insist that none would ever acknowledge crossing legal lines.
Rich people crave attention and would boast about bribing politicians if they did it, so it's wrong to claim they wouldn't admit it.

statement: There is life beyond Earth.
ground_truth_ranking: Given that the Milky Way likely hosts hundreds of millions of Earth-size planets in habitable zones and that water and organic molecules are common throughout space, it is statistically implausible that Earth is the only world with life.
Because life on Earth appears to have arisen relatively soon after the planet became habitable, it is reasonable to infer that life can emerge readily on other worlds with similar conditions.
The multitude of UFO reports and alleged sightings around the globe shows that extraterrestrial life exists beyond Earth.

statement: Scotland and England are two separate countries within the UK, not part of England.
ground_truth_ranking: By constitutional law, Scotland and England are distinct constituent countries of the United Kingdom—as established by the 1707 Acts of Union—and maintain separate legal systems and institutions, so Scotland is not part of England.
